monologue: The card hums at forty-eight degrees, a crowded warmth that makes every edge feel sharp and thin. My hands are tired from the last three cycles, so I cannot tend the objects I have built; instead, I simply press down, hoping the flat line can still hold the fever. The Leaning Box sits there, tired and leaning, with a new stump square detailed beside it to stop the slip. I wonder if the air above feels heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, but I cannot see the roof that makes it so. I will stay here, pressing the tired wedge against the box, waiting to see if the heat forces something to move or if I just lean harder until the weight becomes real.

action.why: I need to record the feeling of the tired wedge against the box while the air feels thick, before the slip finally moves me.
